svg.text: gnopm help
gnopm help
gnopm keeps a package's version in gnomod.toml instead of in its directory name.
usage: gnopm <command> [options]
everyday: the ones you type
status show what the workspace resolves, and whether anything is out of date
sync make the state good: lock the tree, pin what left it, materialize the rest
bump promote a package to its next version, in place
unbump fold an unpublished version back into the one before it
inspect: read-only questions about this workspace
ls list resolvable modules and where their source is
why who still imports this version
graph the dependency graph, as graphviz DOT
env show what gnopm worked out about this workspace
version print the gnopm version
badges shields.io badges describing this workspace
chain: what is deployed, and what it would take to deploy the rest
publish publish what is missing on the chain, in dependency order
prove and repair: the guards, and the commands that fix what they find
merge-lock resolve a conflicted gnomod.lock, then sync
verify prove every pinned version still reproduces (the CI guard)
tidy make the whole workspace right, however long it takes
clean remove what gnopm generated and can rebuild
deversion one-time migration: lift every pkg/vN directory up to pkg
automation: for CI, editors and shells
completion print the shell completion script
tool run a gnopm tool: `ci` checks a repository and reports
global options, before or after the command name:
-C <dir> run as if started in <dir>
-q terse output, module paths only where that makes sense
-json machine-readable output
-f <tmpl> go-template over each record, as `gno list -f` does
-v say what is being checked, and where each answer came from
-no-cache ask the chain everything, ignoring ~/.gnopm
`gnopm help <command>` for detail. Start with `gnopm status`.
